title: Prompt evolution diff format — notes
summary: Working sketch for a compact, patch-based prompt diff format and lightweight API for tracking/rolling out prompt changes across deployments. Emphasis: small cruft, human readable, reversible, rollouts + telemetry hooks.
body:
ALERT: scratchpad. not final.

Goals / constraints:
- Represent changes to 'prompt bundles' (system + templates + tool contracts + examples) as compact deltas.
- Support: preview, apply, revert, merge, conflict resolution.
- API-first: small JSON patch payloads that are easy to instrument, stream, and store in event logs.
- Keep per-change size low (we expect lots of tiny edits).
- Human readable for audits; machine-friendly for rollouts.

Motivation / use cases:
- iterating system prompt wording without shipping full model artifacts
- A/B testing prompt variants across tenants/routes
- patching prompt examples for regressions quickly (hotfix)
- keeping history for evals and rollbacks

Proposed payload model (human sketch):
- top-level: { op, target, meta?, payload }  // op in [insert, replace, remove, move, annotate]
- target: dot-path inside prompt bundle, e.g. "system.instructions", "templates[2].example[1].user"
- payload: string | object depending on op
- meta: author, timestamp, rationale, jira_key, test_prompt_ids

Example patches (line-oriented):
1) small replacement
{
  "op": "replace",
  "target": "system.instructions",
  "payload": "You are an assistant that always asks clarifying Qs BEFORE answering.",
  "meta": { "author": "Evan Carter", "rationale": "reduce hallucination risk", "jira": "JIRA-ENG-9012" }
}

2) insert an example into template 0
{
  "op": "insert",
  "target": "templates[0].examples",
  "payload": { "user": "How do I reset my password?", "assistant": "Step 1..." },
  "meta": { "author": "Maya F", "preview-only": true }
}

API shapes (sketch):
- POST /v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/diffs  -> create a new diff event (accepts list of patch objects). Returns diff_id, preview_url
- GET /v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/diffs/{diff_id} -> fetch details, expanded bundle preview
- POST /v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/rollouts -> { diff_id, targets: [route_id | tenant_id], strategy: { type: canary|gradual|immediate, steps: [...] } }
- POST /v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/diffs/{diff_id}/apply -> server-side apply (blocking/async param)
- POST /v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/diffs/{diff_id}/revert -> revert op that produces inverse patch(s)

Rollout semantics notes:
- diffs are composable but ordering matters. We record base_version for every diff to detect divergent edits.
- preview must render the bundle at base_version + this diff in isolation.
- canary: apply to small tenant subset then expand; telemetry hooks should auto-create eval jobs (quality / regression tests)

Patch merge / conflict rules (rough):
- If two replace ops touch same exact target -> conflict. Prefer last-write-by-author? better: require manual merge if different authors.
- If one op removes and another replaces same target -> mark conflict.
- For arrays (templates/examples) we recommend stable ids for elements to avoid index-based collisions.

Local apply algorithm (pseudocode bullet):
- load bundle at base_version
- for each patch in diff.patches:
  - resolve target path to node (support dot notation + bracket numeric OR stable-id lookups)
  - validate op vs node type (insert only allowed into array or map)
  - apply op, record inverse op to allow revert
- compute resulting bundle hash, store as preview

Storage model & history:
- store diffs as first-class objects (small), store snapshots rarely (every N diffs or on release)
- provide compact change log for audits: diff_id, author, rationale, hashed preview, tests triggered

Telemetry hooks / evals:
- diff creation triggers: quick synthetic eval (smoke), optional full eval queue (longer), and canary profiling for latency/cost regressions
- record token delta estimates (simple tokenization diff heuristic) to surface cost impact in rollout UI

Security / trust boundaries:
- diffs for private / tenant-scoped bundles inherit tenant ACLs; server must prevent cross-tenant patching
- meta.author must be an org user id (resolve via SSO)
- signed diffs? optionally support signing for high-sensitivity tenants (airgap scenario)

Examples / edge cases to think about:
- binary attachments in templates (images) -> diffs should reference external object ids rather than embed base64
- large reformatting (massive replace) -> prefer snapshot flow instead of large diff chain
- non-deterministic placeholders in templates ({{date}}) -> diffs that change formatting rules may need staged rollout to avoid user-facing churn

Unresolved / TODOs:
- path grammar: supporting both numeric indices and stable-id lookups. need spec.
- how to produce inverse ops for complex transforms (e.g., split + reorder) automatically? fallback: require manual revert id that references a snapshot.
- conflict resolution UX in Console: inline merge editor vs always require local edit + reapply.
- should we adopt an existing patch format (JSON Patch RFC6902) or a custom smaller DSL tuned for prompts? tradeoffs: RFC6902 is standard but verbose for arrays of examples.
- coordinate with optimize team: token-delta estimation accuracy and how to integrate quantized-cost heuristics.

Next steps / actionable:
- get quick alignment w/ product (Priya) about ops allowed in drafts vs released bundles (ie restrict certain ops on released templates)
- prototype server parser for our mini-DSL + inverse op generator (week spike) -> add unit tests for common transforms
- wire up minimal POST /diffs endpoint with store + preview generation (no rollout UI yet)
- draft console UX for canary step config (simple percentage/time based)

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- think of diffs as "textual code-reviews" for prompts. treat prompts as code with PR workflows (but lighter-weight).
- tagging patches with evaluation suites will be key to avoiding accidental quality regressions.
- small diffs + many evaluations -> need cheap smoke eval path to keep costs down.

References:
- RFC6902 JSON Patch (for inspiration)
- internal: JIRA-ENG-9012 (prompt-hotfix backfill), GH PR proto link above

End of scratchpad.
